Where a field written by an event starts in its details

log_field_at.Rd

REDCap logs an edit as field = 'value', the fields apart by a comma and a space or a line break. So a field starts at the start of details, or right after a comma, and its name is followed by = and the apostrophe that opens the value. Searched anywhere in details, as before 2026-11-12, a field name matched inside the value of another field: the channel's Read back as, applied_as = 'role_name=...; dag_name=...; expiration=...' (round_applied_as()), read as a write of all three, measured on 2026-11-12 (M1b) on 46 events out of 102 that "wrote" role_name, on every row of the register. The name has to be followed by the apostrophe too, which a value that quotes name= does not carry.

Usage

log_field_at(fields)

Arguments

fields

Field names, one or more.

Value

A regular expression, Perl syntax, that matches up to and including the apostrophe that opens the value.

Details

What it cannot tell apart is a value that holds ', field = ' itself: the log does not escape an apostrophe inside a value, and no reading of the text can say where such a value ends.

The one pattern every reader of a field in details starts from: log_wrote(), log_value(), log_written_value(), and the check of a whole value in log_change_authors().
